GROW WEST WALNUT GROVE
RMP EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

ES-1.0  FACILITY ACCIDENTAL RELEASE POLICY

The owners, management, and employees of the Walnut Grove Retail, part of Grow West (herein referred to as Walnut Grove or the Walnut Grove Facility) at 14301 Railroad Ave, Walnut Grove, California 95690 are committed to the prevention of an accidental release of anhydrous ammonia. If an accidental release should occur, the Facility is prepared to work with the local fire department, or other authorities, to mitigate any release and minimize the impact of the release to people and the environment. A detailed Emergency Action Plan - Consolidated Contingency Plan (EAP-CCP) has been developed and will be implemented in the event of an accidental release.


ES-2.0  FACILITY INFORMATION

The Facility is a retail agricultural facility whose primary activity is the sale and distribution of fertilizers in addition to the sale of pre-packaged agricultural chemicals to agricultural operations in the Sacramento Delta Area of Northern California. Applicable NAICS codes for this facility include 424910 (Farm Supplies Merchant Wholesalers). Specific information about the Grow West Walnut Grove facility is as follows: 

- Anhydrous ammonia (NH3) is received, stored, and distributed for direct application as crop production nutrients. 
- Anhydrous ammonia is received by truck and stored in a 14,323 gallon storage tank (bullet).
- Anhydrous ammonia is loaded-out to US DOT Nurse Tanks, with a 1,000-gallon shell volume, when ordered by customers. Nurse Tanks are not used to store ammonia. 
- The anhydrous ammonia vessels (i.e., storage vessel and mobile tanks) are filled to no more than 85% of shell volume. 

ANHYDROUS AMMONIA BULLET 
- Vessel Capacity: 14,323 gals
- Maximum Amount of NH3: 12,175 gals
- Mass of NH3: 62,580 lbs (density of 5.14 lbs/gal)

The maximum quantity of anhydrous ammonia handled at the Walnut Grove Facility is 62,580 pounds.


ES-3.0  ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION PROGRAM

The Facility has implemented the following prevention program elements.

PROCESS SAFETY INFORMATION:  Walnut Grove Retail ensures that information concerning covered processes and regulated substances are up-to-date and available for review by employees. Information compiled includes chemical data, equipment data, information regarding the handling process, piping diagrams, consequences of process deviation, safety systems, etc. 

PROCESS HAZARD ANALYSIS:  A review of the anhydrous ammonia process is conducted every five years or as needed by changes in the processes. Grow West has in place a process to address hazards associated with the anhydrous ammonia system. Results indicate that no high-risk hazards were identified through the hazard review updates.

OPERATING PROCEDURES:  Written standard operating procedures have been developed for the covered process and are reviewed annually and revised as needed. Procedures address each phase of operations (load-in, load-out, inspections, etc.) and also address each operating limits, safety and health, and emergency equipment and systems. 

TRAINING:  The Walnut Grove Retail Facility staff, as well as Grow West corporate staff, understands that incidents involving the accidental release of regulated substances can be reduced by having trained operations and maintenance staff. A training program, which incorporates specific operating procedures and safe work practices, is an essential element of an effective prevention program. 

The current training program is comprised of the following:
1.  Initial employee training;
2.  Periodic refresher training;
3.  Training provided as a result of a new equipment addition or modification;
4.  Competency testing involving written tests and observation following training; and
5.  Training records for each employee.

MECHANICAL INTEGRITY:  The mechanical integrity program at the Facility is intended to preserve the process equipment in optimum condition to minimize the potential for

an accidental release. The program includes comprehensive equipment information, equipment inspection, preventative maintenance, recordkeeping, and training. 

MANAGEMENT OF CHANGE:  Operation, safety, and environmental issues must be reviewed prior to initiation of a process change to ensure that they do not compromise the operational safety and integrity of the Anhydrous Ammonia Process, and to minimize adverse effects to worker safety and public health. The Management of Change (MOC) process is used to evaluate all changes to process materials, controls, equipment, and procedures.

PRE START-UP SAFETY REVIEW:  The pre start-up safety review (PSSR) applies to additions or modifications to the Anhydrous Ammonia Process that require the safety information to be revised or updated. Whenever changes in affected processes are identified or planned, they must be evaluated as to the need for a pre start-up safety review. This assessment is undertaken in conjunction with the MOC review. Additionally, a pre start-up safety review is performed in conjunction with the MOC review when the proposed change requires modifications to the safety procedures. 

COMPLIANCE AUDITS:  Periodic compliance audits to assess the effectiveness of the written plan must be conducted every three years. Records of the audits and follow-up documentation are maintained to indicate findings and resolution of findings. 

INCIDENT INVESTIGATION:  Although no incidents involving regulated substances have occurred at the Facility in the last five years, an incident investigation program is in place. The program includes investigation requirements and reporting and would be implemented in the event of an incident.

EMPLOYEE PARTICIPATION:  Grow West Walnut Groves relies upon the operational expertise and training of its employees at all levels and disciplines to ensure safe operations. Grow West Walnut Grove has an Employee Participation Program in place and has implemented procedures regarding engaging

employees for their input, as well as providing access to safety documentation to ensure consideration of their knowledge and experience in all applicable areas of the prevention program. Operators are included in the process hazards analysis, emergency planning, and in the development of procedures. Employees are encouraged to review the RMP. 

HOT WORK PERMIT:  With regard to hot work that may occur on or near the Anhydrous Ammonia Process, Grow West has developed a written Hot Work Permit program and procedure to document the evaluation and implementation of the fire prevention and protection requirements. 

CONTRACTOR SAFETY:  The contractors used by the Facility for anhydrous ammonia delivery have been informed regarding the known potential fire, explosion, or toxic release hazards related to delivery of anhydrous ammonia to the Grow West Walnut Grove. The Facility has confirmed that the delivery contractors have provided the appropriate training to their drivers regarding the delivery of anhydrous ammonia. Grow West Walnut Grove also qualifies contractors who are engaged in maintaining the RS systems to ensure that equipment is modified or repaired and returned to service safely. 

OTHER CODE APPLICABILITY:  The Facility implements the provisions of the following guidelines, regulations, and standards for these regulated substances (partial list):
Regulated Substances

- United States Department of Labor, Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), 29 CFR 1910.38, Employee emergency response plan and fire prevention plans
- United States Environmental Protection Agency (US EPA), 40 CFR Chapter 1, Subchapter C, Part 68, Subpart E, Emergency Response
- United States Department of Labor, Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), 29 CFR 1910.111, Storage and Handling of Anhydrous Ammonia
- California Code of Regulations, Title 8, Division 1, Chapter 4, Subchapter 1, Unfired Pressure Vessel Safety Orders
- Compressed Gas Association (CGA) Req

uirements for Storage and Handling of Anhydrous Ammonia, CGA 2.1-2023 edition
- American Society of Mechanical Engineers (pressure vessel and process piping) 
- California Fire Code, Chapter 50, Hazardous Materials


ES-4.0  FIVE-YEAR ACCIDENT HISTORY
There have been no accidental releases of anhydrous ammonia during the last five years resulting in death, injuries, evacuation(s), a shelter in-place order, or property or environmental damage.


ES-5.0  THE EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROGRAM
The facility's emergency response program is developed in accordance with Section 25503, Division 6.95 of the California Health and Safety Code, Hazardous Materials Business Plan requirements. The facility also developed an Emergency Response Program in accordance with the requirements presented in the CalARP regulations in Article 8. Grow West has developed an Emergency Action Plan - Consolidated Contingency Plan (EAP-CCP) that encompasses the requirements of the CalARP Emergency Response Program, and that EAP-CCP is updated annually and will be implemented in the event of an accidental release of a regulated substance. Employees are trained in implementing the EAP-CCP. 


ES-6.0  PLANNED CHANGES TO IMPROVE SAFETY
Safety improvement is an on-going process at the Facility. Periodic evaluations will be performed to assess the maintenance of safe conditions. Specific changes to the anhydrous ammonia process at the Facility will be implemented as needed.


ES-7.0  THE WORST-CASE RELEASE AND ALTERNATIVE RELEASE SCENARIOS
Anhydrous Ammonia Worst-Case and Alternative Release Scenarios. The worst-case release scenario is the failure of the storage tank when filled to the greatest amount, which would release 62,580 pounds of anhydrous ammonia over a 10-minute period; this represents the volume of the storage tank administratively limited at 85% of capacity. The alternative release scenario, based on the hazard review (or a more plausible potential incident), is a release from a broken 2-inch dia

meter pipe (or transfer hose) with an increased wind speed and "D" stability modeling parameters. The alternative release scenario assumes that approximately 11,900 pounds of ammonia would be released as a result of a break during a two-minute release event.
